feasibility_reasoning:
The mechanism is sound in principle. React 19 Float precedence resources are already in use (widgetStyleSheets.tsx:1-39). charts.css has no @layer or Tailwind directives, so the layer order is unchanged. Fizz emits precedence sheets before the core <link>, the same cascade slot as today's @import at styles.css:19.

The change breaks because the --chart-* palette has consumers outside ChartFrame, features/* and PolicyPositionsMap:
- Public route src/routes/tracker.explorer.tsx:264 (legend) and :353 (every cell of the stance matrix) set style={{backgroundColor: hex, background: var(--chart-positive|negative|2|axis)}} (euCountries.ts:85-106). The route renders no chart component. With the palette gone from the core, the shorthand is invalid at computed-value time and the colour becomes transparent, so the matrix loses its colours.
- Admin screens: KpiTile.tsx:160 stroke=var(--chart-1) with no fallback (used by about 11 admin screens), DeltaBadge.tsx:26-27, DashboardSection.tsx:111, RealtimeStrip.tsx:71-82, and the DataVizBlocks.tsx:382,777 editor swatches. admin.tsx:66-67 links only admin-styles.css.
- The tests palette.test.ts:65-72, pieChart.test.tsx:1124, choroplethMap.test.tsx:438,758 and geometry.test.ts:38 cut the token blocks at the first ':root,' / '.dark {' / '@layer base' of styles.css+charts.css. Once the tokens move, they land after @layer base and the lookups fail. charts.css:640-642 documents this cut.
- Doctrine: the split was reverted twice (fa67890; d02c50f added styles.css:17-19, 'keep chart rules beside the shared palette'). check-bundle-size.ts:2017-2021 says the chart tokens must stay in the shared sheet.
blocking_issues: /tracker/explorer (public): legend and matrix swatches use var(--chart-*) via the inline background shorthand (tracker.explorer.tsx:264,353) and render no chart component, so they would become transparent

Palette gate tests (palette/pieChart/choroplethMap/geometry) slice the first :root,/.dark/@layer base blocks of styles.css+charts.css and would fail; the block cut must be rewritten

Doctrine conflict and twice-reverted history (fa67890, d02c50f; styles.css:17-19; check-bundle-size.ts:2017-2021) mean it can only land together with C11 and a kronika entry; the publicCss sum rises by about +0.5 KB

effect_reasoning:
Marginal savings measured with postcss on the built styles-DjfYz07w.css: palette declarations (326 light + 322 dark --chart-*) plus the .neh-* rules come to 26.9 KB raw / 6.0 KB gzip-6 / 4.1 KB br-11. The claimed 6.6 KB is the area's gzip on its own. The area attribution of 29.5 KB counts the whole :root,.light rule (9 282 B, including 1 743 B of brand tokens) and the whole .dark rule (8 417 B, including 994 B of brand tokens). tiers2's stage-1 simulation also drops the full .dark rule, which overstates stage 1.

Lantern mobile, using the analyst model (LCP about 0.9 s + 6 ms/KB of the pre-LCP set): PSI transfer is roughly gzip, so -6 KB gives LCP about -36 ms. FCP is JS-bound today (analyst what-if: CSS -70 % gives FCP 0 ms), so FCP is about 0 now and about -31 ms after boot-js:C3. Fixture br elasticity of 4-6 ms/KB times 4.1 KB gives -16 to -25 ms.

Score from the log-normal curves (FCP weight 10, LCP 25, SI 10): +0.06 pt in the PSI-prod state (LCP 6.6 s), +0.12 to 0.21 on the fixture today, +0.32 after the plan lands (LCP about 2.9 s). Cross-check: CSS -70 % (49 KB) measured +3 pts, which is 0.061 pt/KB, so 6 KB gives +0.37 pt. Desktop: 0.8 ms/KB times 6 KB is about -5 ms, so 0 pt.

This is below the noise of measure-ab at n=3 (A-arm medians wander by 10-30 ms). I ran no what-if, because the HTML transform cannot swap the CSS asset, and the structural number is tighter than any run would be.
corrected_estimate: Core sheet -26.9 KB raw / -6.0 KB gzip-6 / -4.1 KB br (not -29.5 / -6.6). Mobile LCP -20 to -36 ms; FCP 0 today and about -30 ms after boot-js:C3; +0.1 to +0.3 mobile points; desktop 0. Its only real value is as part of the stage-1 render-blocking diet. Split: palette tokens 3.5 KB gz / 2.1 KB br; engine rules 1.9 KB gz / 1.5 KB br.
better_alternative: Move only the chart engine rules (drop the @import at styles.css:19 and load charts.css through a Float link) and keep the --chart-* tokens in the core. That avoids the tracker/admin breakage and the test re-cut, at the cost of a smaller saving (1.9 KB gz, about -10 ms).
